title: fix: review-bot-gate passes on rate-limit/quota warnings without actual code review
body:
## Problem

When CodeRabbit or Gemini post rate-limit/quota warning comments on a PR, the `review-bot-gate-helper.sh` reports `PASS` (bots have posted) and the `Wait for AI Review Bots` CI check passes. However, no actual code review occurred — the bots posted error messages, not reviews.

## Observed pattern (2026-03-07)

17 PRs across marcusquinn/aidevops, marcusquinn/aidevops.sh, and marcusquinn/turbostarter-plus all have:
- `review-bot-gate-helper.sh` returning `PASS` (found: coderabbitai gemini-code-assist)
- Formal review count = 0 (no actual reviews)
- CodeRabbit comment: "Rate limit exceeded" 
- Gemini comment: "You have reached your daily quota limit"

The formal review count gate (=0) correctly blocks auto-merge. But the gate check misleadingly reports PASS, which could confuse future pulse logic or human reviewers.

## Root cause

`review-bot-gate-helper.sh` detects bot presence by checking for bot usernames in PR comments. It does not distinguish between rate-limit warnings and actual review comments.

## Proposed fix

In `review-bot-gate-helper.sh`, when a bot comment is found, check whether it contains rate-limit/quota warning patterns (e.g., "Rate limit exceeded", "daily quota limit"). If so, treat it as `WAITING` rather than `PASS` — the bot acknowledged the PR but did not review it.

Alternatively, check for the presence of a CodeRabbit review summary (the `<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: summarize by coderabbit.ai -->` marker combined with actual review content, not just the rate-limit template).

## Impact

Low urgency — the formal review count gate prevents incorrect merges. But the misleading PASS status adds confusion and may cause future pulse logic to incorrectly conclude bots have reviewed when they haven't.
